analysis.title: USA: New York Fed President Williams Says Inflation Is "Stubbornly High" but Situation Doesn't Call for "Dramatic Action"
key_insights: NY Fed President Williams said "inflation is stubbornly high and we need to get it down" but "I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action" when asked about a 50bp hike at the December meeting, an option Governor Waller raised last week.
Williams described the firmer-than-expected October core CPI print as a "continuation," not a "broadening," of the passthrough from tariffs and the energy shock into prices.

Williams called AI an "important" driver of inflation that is "more likely to be the persistent factor" going forward. GS estimates AI-related price pressure on year-over-year core PCE inflation peaks at the end of 2026 and declines gradually through 2027 as memory price growth slows.

Vice Chair Jefferson said further policy adjustments should be determined by examining "trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks." GS reads the focus on "trends" as hinting at a more gradual pace of hikes.

Cleveland Fed President Hammack said it is "important to put restriction back in the economy" and prefers slow, steady increments at successive meetings. St. Louis Fed President Musalem said the economy will likely require several rate increases before spring 2027 to reach 2% inflation in a timely manner.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The NY Fed president, Jefferson and Hammack lean toward a gradual pace of hikes. Waller raised 50bp and Musalem expects several hikes before spring 2027.

risk_factors: Inflation is stubbornly high, with passthrough from tariffs and the energy shock still feeding into prices.
AI-related price pressure, particularly memory prices, is a persistent inflation driver according to Williams.
Hawkish dispersion among FOMC participants, from Waller's 50bp option to Musalem's several hikes before spring 2027, leaves the pace of tightening uncertain.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish side: Waller raised a 50bp hike in December, and Musalem sees several hikes needed before spring 2027 to reach 2% inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Gradual side: Williams sees no need for dramatic action, Jefferson stresses "trends in the data" which GS reads as a more gradual pace, and Hammack prefers slow, steady increments.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further firm core inflation prints that show a broadening of price pressure beyond tariff, energy and AI passthrough, which Williams said October did not show.
